web search 2026-10-22: no City of Roundup or chamber page for the campground; only Campendium, RoverPass and AllStays listings

values.note: No camping fee is posted; 'Donations for maintenance are accepted in the donation post on the west entrance.' Events may rent the roped-off area ($25).

fees.source: https://musselshellcounty.gov/fairgrounds ('Cow Bells Campground is for public use ... Donations for maintenance are accepted in the donation post on the west entrance'; fee schedule 'Cow Bells Campground (roped off area) – $25' for event use), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Public campground at the county fairgrounds; events may use portions of it but may not close it to the public. Trailers, tents and vehicles may not be left unattended over 48 hours.

booking.source: https://musselshellcounty.gov/fairgrounds ('Camping longer than 14 days is prohibited', 'cannot be left unattended for over 48 hours', 'No activities will be allowed to close off the campground to the public'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Restrooms (comfort stations) open seasonally, usually mid to late May through early to mid September; the county shuts the water off on October 8, closing the comfort stations.

facilities.source: https://musselshellcounty.gov/fairgrounds ('Restrooms are only open seasonally during warm weather. (Usually mid to late May through the 1st to mid September ...)', 'The water will be shut off on October 8th which will close the use of the comfort stations'), read 2026-10-22. The stored drinking-water value was derived from a note resting on directory listings; the county page mentions water only for the comfort stations, so it is cleared.

hookups.source: The county page says nothing about electric hookups; the stored 'no electric' was derived from a note resting on directory listings (Campendium), so it is cleared (read 2026-10-22).

sites.source: The county page gives no site count; the stored ~35 rests on Campendium, so it is cleared (read 2026-10-22).

note: Musselshell County's Cow Belles (Cow Bells) Campground at the county fairgrounds in Roundup, by the Musselshell River: shaded drive-in sites under cottonwoods, some along the riverbank. Directory listings (not the county) describe about 35 unmarked sites with water and no electric. --Claude
